story: Roger Penrose – Is Mathematics Invented or Discovered? [video]
text: Recently I watched Sixty Symbols video on why light is slower in glass and there are multiple explanations on it. What struck me was what prof. Michael Merrifield said at the end of his explanation: [VIDEO] On the question about what is the reality, what explanation is the true one, Merrifield said that the Math works on all of the explanations and what those explanations do is simply to model the behaviour of nature and not necessarily reflect the reality. That's how Newtonian physics and relativistic physics are both correct models, tools to model nature and simply can be used to whenever suitable. Wouldn't that mean that mathematics is just an invented tool to reason about physical models?

story: Do we really travel through time with the speed of light?
text: downvoted because time traveling through a medium vs traveling through curved space are not anywhere near the same underlying principles[0]. The implication being suggested is - if I was trapped in a block of plastic or... underwater, I would experience time different compared to someone standing on land just because "c" is slower. Clearly not the case. To be specific, when "the speed of light" is discussed like this, it usually means the "speed of causality"[1] which is the underlying meaning of "c" in relativity. The speed of causality through a medium (i.e. water) is the same as a vacuum if spacetime curvature is the same. [0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK]

Absorption and re-emission are probabilistic, so you'd expect experiments to show a spread distribution of propagation times, deflection angles, etc that aren't actually observed. The explanation gets into looking at light as a wave. [VIDEO] [LINK]
